title: Model-mix cost ladder and hiring-trigger notes
content:
Executive summary:

This is a working workbook to translate expected customer workload shifts (model mix + burstiness) into a cost ladder and hiring trigger plan. Purpose: give finance, product and infra a compact view of (a) incremental $/token by model mix and quantization decisions, (b) headcount phasing tied to throughput breakpoints, and (c) a small set of pricing sensitivity rules that signal when to nudge customers or accelerate hiring/capacity. Not final — intended for planning conversation w/ infra and product ops.

Key assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline month: May 2026. Current steady-state tokens: 4.2B tokens/month. Growth runway scenarios use 6/12/24 month horizons.
- Current model mix (tokens): 60% lightweight chat models (L2), 30% mid-size rerank/embeddings (M1), 10% large context generation (L4).
- Unit infra costs (effective delivered after discounts & amort): GPU-hour blended = $10/hr (weighted fleet mix), instance efficiency factor by model: L2=0.35, M1=0.7, L4=3.5 (relative GPU hr per million tokens).
- Average price per 1k tokens charged (hosted): L2 = $0.004, M1 = $0.025, L4 = $0.20.
- Avg headcount ramp cost: new infra hire (infra engineer/SRE) fully loaded = $28k/mo (salary + overhead amortized monthly), product/ops PM = $20k/mo, MLE scale hire = $22k/mo.
- Hiring lead time: 10–12 weeks to productive. Contracting burst capacity (spot/partner) premium = +45% per unit.

Cost ladder snapshot (per-million tokens):
- L2: infra cost = $10/hr * 0.35 * (1 / 1) = $3.5 per million tokens; margin at current price = 0.004*1000 - 3.5 = $4 - $3.5 = $0.5 per million tokens (thin).
- M1: infra cost = $10 * 0.7 = $7.0 per million; revenue = $0.025*1000 = $25; margin = $18 per million tokens.
- L4: infra cost = $10 * 3.5 = $35 per million; revenue = $200; margin = $165 per million tokens.

Note: cost numbers are illustrative and include runtime inefficiency buffer (10%). If we apply 8-bit quantization profile to L4 with 25% throughput improvement, cost per million drops from $35 -> $28, improving margin by ~$7/million. But quality/regression risk must be evaluated per customer cohort.

Scenario blocks (three scenarios):
1) Base growth (conservative): +25% tokens in 12m, model mix stable.
2) Model-shift (mid): +45% tokens; L4 share rises to 20% (new multimodal customer wins).
3) Price-compression downside: +20% tokens but effective price per 1k tokens down 12% due to competitive pressure and enterprise discounting.

Headcount trigger logic (draft):
- Trigger A (throughput): If tokens/mo > 5.5B for two consecutive months, hire 2 infra/SREs and 1 infra MLE (ramp +12 weeks). Rationale: sustained throughput increases ops toil and necessitates dedicated capacity tuning.
- Trigger B (model complexity): If L4 share > 15% of tokens, add 1 model-ops and 1 infra-specialist with quantization experience. Rationale: L4 increases tail-latency and KV/cache requirements.
- Trigger C (capacity margin): If spot/partner usage > 20% of peak capacity for >3 weeks, accelerate contracting or hire 1 capacity manager and budget +$120k for reserved capacity.

Projected P&L delta examples (rounded):
- Base: +25% tokens -> incremental gross margin = weighted margin * incremental tokens. Weighted margin baseline = (0.6*0.5 + 0.3*18 + 0.1*165) = 20.25 per million tokens. Additional 1.05B tokens (25% of 4.2B) -> incremental gross = 21.26k (i.e., 1.05B/1M * 20.25). After hiring (2 infra hires + 1 PM) add ~$78k/mo in SG&A; still strongly accretive at base.
- Model-shift: L4 doubles from 10% to 20%, total tokens +45% -> margin improves due to higher L4 weight but capex and reserved GPU commitments increase: need 4 reserved GPU pools -> additional committed cost $420k/yr. Net present margin still positive but requires commitment capital.
- Price-compression downside: 12% lower realized price reduces weighted margin from ~20.25 -> ~17.82 per million tokens. With +20% tokens, net incremental gross shrinks; break-even headcount triggers later.

Pricing sensitivity rules (operationalized):
- Elasticity quick test: run A/B on 5% price increase for low-cost L2 customers (volume < 50M tokens/mo). If churn < 0.8% and revenue/ token increases, extend across cohort. If churn > 1.5% then revert.
- Tier nudges: For customers whose model mix is >75% L2 and discount >20%, auto-suggest caching + batch controls and apply minimum per-request fee equivalent to $0.002 per 1k tokens for very small requests.
- Enterprise negotiation floor: any multi-year commitment with >$500k ARR must include a scheduled throughput audit at months 3 and 9; pricing floors can be re-negotiated if usage shifts >40% in model mix towards L4/M1.

Quick runbook for infra/product handoff:
1) Weekly: publish current tokens by model-class (rolling 8-week window) to the capacity dashboard.
2) If Trigger A/B/C hit, finance owner and infra lead convene within 72 hours to sign-off on hiring/contracting plan and budget reallocation.
3) Pre-commit checklist for reserved GPU pools: 6-week notice, expected utilization >70% in 3 months, fallback plan to partner burst if under 60%.

Open questions & risks (items to resolve in next 2 weeks):
- Validate model-specific efficiency multipliers against latest serving runtime telemetry (SLA adjustments changed in March 2026); current multipliers are still using pre-optimizations.
- Confirm hire lead time and sourcing capacity; vendor contracting (spot partners) has 3-week onboarding vs 10–12 weeks for FTEs which affects trigger choice.
- Risk: Pricing erosion from emerging competitor offering near-L2 performance at 20% lower price — need churn elasticity experiment scoped by GTM.

Action items (owners):
- Priya: run unit-cost re-compile with March runtime kernels and update the L2/L4 efficiency numbers. Due: 2026-05-04.
- Marco: add the model-class tokens feed to the capacity dashboard (rolling 8-week). Due: 2026-04-23.
- Leah: scope a 5% price increase A/B test for L2 cohort; draft comms and rollback plan. Due: 2026-05-15.
- Ethan: confirm partner burst contract terms (45% premium estimate) and vendor SLAs. Due: 2026-04-30.

Appendix (example micro-table, text-format):
Tokens/month bands | Action | Estimated incremental monthly cost | Hiring implication
-------------------|--------|-------------------------------|-------------------
< 4.8B | status quo | +$0 | none
4.8B - 5.5B | monitor | +$40k (spot) | prepare reqs
5.5B - 7.5B | reserve capacity | +$120k (reserved amort) | hire 2 infra, 1 MLE
> 7.5B | capacity expansion + HQ | +$420k | hire + infra lead, PM, 2 MLEs

Notes: tables above are rough and intentionally conservative on hiring to avoid premature FTE commits. We prefer to use a mix of rapid contracting + incremental FTEs once utilization stabilizes.

End of working notes.

Document history: created 2026-04-12 by Priya Raman; draft shared with Marco/Leah/Ethan for comment.
